questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What is the water potential of pure water at 298 K and 101.3 kPa?
questions.hint: It is the reference value.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: State a unit used for water potential.
questions.hint: It is a unit of pressure.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In which direction does water move by osmosis?
options: From lower to higher water potential
From higher to lower water potential
Always from lower to higher pressure potential
questions.answer: From higher to lower water potential
questions.hint: Compare this to a gradient that runs downhill.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What effect does adding solutes have on the solute potential of water?
questions.hint: Solutes reduce the tendency of water to move.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: State the term for a solution with a higher solute concentration than the cell.
questions.hint: The prefix means 'above'.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A plant cell has a solute potential of −800 kPa and a pressure potential of +300 kPa. Calculate its water potential in kPa.
questions.hint: Add the two components, keeping their signs.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A plant cell has a water potential of −450 kPa and a solute potential of −700 kPa. Calculate its pressure potential in kPa.
questions.hint: Rearrange the water potential equation.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A plant cell with a solute potential of −600 kPa is placed in pure water and reaches equilibrium. Calculate its pressure potential in kPa.
questions.hint: At equilibrium, the cell's water potential equals that of pure water.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Cell A has a water potential of −400 kPa and adjacent cell B has −700 kPa. What is the net movement of water?
options: Equal in both directions, with solutes moving to A
questions.hint: Identify the higher water potential. Remember that −400 is greater than −700.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A plant cell with a water potential of −300 kPa is placed in a solution of −500 kPa. What happens?
options: Water enters and pressure potential rises
Water leaves and pressure potential falls
There is no net movement of water
questions.answer: Water leaves and pressure potential falls
questions.hint: Compare the two values, then think about the wall.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What is the approximate pressure potential of a fully plasmolysed plant cell?
questions.hint: The membrane is no longer pressing against the wall.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Where in a plant is a negative pressure potential commonly found?
options: In the sap under tension in xylem
In the vacuole of a turgid root cell
questions.answer: In the sap under tension in xylem
questions.hint: Think about transpiration pull.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Why does an animal cell in a hypotonic solution burst rather than reach a high pressure potential?
options: It has no cell wall to resist expansion
It has a very high solute potential
Its water potential is always zero
questions.answer: It has no cell wall to resist expansion
questions.hint: What in a plant cell allows pressure potential to build up?

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Plant tissue has a mass of 12.5 g before and 11.0 g after being placed in a solution. Calculate the percentage change in mass. Use a minus sign for a loss.
questions.hint: Divide the change in mass by the initial mass.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A plant cell has been placed in a hypotonic solution. Explain, using solute potential and pressure potential, how its water potential changes as it takes in water.
questions.hint: Consider how each component changes as water enters.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Design an experiment to determine the water potential of potato tissue. Include the variables, how the results would be processed, and how the value would be obtained.
questions.hint: Think of a range of solutions with known water potentials, and the point of no mass change.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Which statement defines osmosis?
options: Net movement of water across a partially permeable membrane to a higher solute concentration
Movement of solutes across a membrane to a lower solute concentration
Active movement of water using ATP
Movement of water through xylem to the leaves
questions.answer: Net movement of water across a partially permeable membrane to a higher solute concentration
questions.hint: Focus on what moves and through what.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: State the term for a solution with a lower solute concentration than the cell's cytoplasm.
questions.hint: The prefix means 'below'.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: State the term for a solution with the same solute concentration as the cell's cytoplasm.
questions.hint: The prefix means 'equal'.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What happens to an animal cell placed in distilled water?
options: It takes in water and may burst
questions.answer: It takes in water and may burst
questions.hint: The cytoplasm has more solutes than distilled water.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: What happens to a plant cell placed in a hypertonic solution?
options: The membrane pulls away from the cell wall
It gains water and becomes turgid
questions.answer: The membrane pulls away from the cell wall
questions.hint: Water leaves the cell.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: State the name of the process in which a plant cell's membrane pulls away from its wall as water is lost.
questions.hint: Think about what happens to the cytoplasm as it shrinks.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Why does a plant cell not burst in a hypotonic solution?
options: Its cell wall resists further expansion
Its membrane is impermeable to water
It pumps all water out using ATP
questions.answer: Its cell wall resists further expansion
questions.hint: Which structure do plant cells have that animal cells lack?

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: State the term for the pressure of cell contents against a plant cell wall.
questions.hint: Think about a firm plant cell that is not wilting.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Why are organs for transplant kept in a cold isotonic solution?
options: To prevent net water gain or loss by the cells
To provide the cells with oxygen
To stop bacteria from reproducing by osmosis
To dissolve the blood in the vessels
questions.answer: To prevent net water gain or loss by the cells
questions.hint: Consider what hypotonic and hypertonic solutions would do to tissue.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A potato cylinder has a mass of 5.0 g before and 5.6 g after being placed in a sucrose solution. Calculate the percentage change in mass.
questions.hint: Divide the change in mass by the initial mass.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A potato cylinder has a mass of 8.0 g before and 6.8 g after being placed in a sucrose solution. Calculate the percentage change in mass. Use a minus sign for a loss.
questions.hint: Divide the change in mass by the initial mass.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In an osmosis practical, why is percentage change in mass used rather than change in mass?
options: The cylinders may have different initial masses
It removes the need for a balance
Mass cannot be measured accurately in grams
It increases the rate of osmosis
questions.answer: The cylinders may have different initial masses
questions.hint: Think about making fair comparisons.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: In a practical testing tissue in a range of sucrose solutions, which is the independent variable?
questions.hint: It is the factor deliberately changed by the investigator.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: A graph shows no change in mass of tissue at 0.3 mol dm⁻³ sucrose. What does this suggest?
options: The solution is isotonic with the tissue
questions.answer: The solution is isotonic with the tissue
questions.hint: What does no net water movement imply?

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Outline a method to estimate the solute concentration of potato tissue using a range of sucrose solutions. Include how you would control variables and process your results.
questions.hint: Think about the range of solutions, controlled variables, measurements and the graph.

questions.subject: bio
questions.q: Explain why intravenous fluids given to patients must be isotonic with blood plasma, referring to the effects of hypotonic and hypertonic solutions on red blood cells.
questions.hint: Consider both possible errors separately.

bus-hl.topic: Organizational structure — HL: project-based structures and Handy's shamrock

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In Handy's shamrock organization, how many groups make up the workforce?
questions.hint: Consider the leaves of the plant.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In Handy's shamrock, which group contains the essential permanent managers and specialists?
questions.hint: They are central to the organization's knowledge.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which group of Handy's shamrock is made up of part-time and temporary workers?
questions.hint: Their hours rise and fall with demand.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: In Handy's shamrock, what is the contractual fringe?
options: External specialists who provide outsourced services
questions.answer: External specialists who provide outsourced services
questions.hint: These people work for a fee, not a wage.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What characterizes a project-based organization?
options: Work is arranged around teams formed for specific projects
Each employee does the same task permanently
All decisions are taken by the founder
Departments are fixed by function forever
questions.answer: Work is arranged around teams formed for specific projects
questions.hint: Teams come together for a task and then disband.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A key benefit of a project-based structure for a consultancy is:
options: Specialists can be brought together flexibly for each client
Job roles never need to change
There is no need for managers to coordinate
questions.answer: Specialists can be brought together flexibly for each client
questions.hint: Think about how client needs differ.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A key drawback of project-based work for employees is:
options: Reduced job security when projects end
questions.answer: Reduced job security when projects end
questions.hint: Consider what happens after the final deadline.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: State the term for moving part of a firm's work to an external supplier, as used in Handy's contractual fringe.
questions.hint: The task moves outside the business.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A firm has 1 director, 5 managers each with a span of control of 7, and each manager's team is made up only of front-line staff. Calculate the total number of employees including the director and managers.
questions.hint: Find the front-line staff first.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which pair correctly matches a structure with a likely characteristic?
options: Flat structure: narrow spans of control
Matrix structure: one line manager only
questions.hint: Count how many people a message passes through.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Why might a business with an uncertain demand choose the shamrock model?
options: It can adjust labour costs quickly
It guarantees permanent jobs for all
It removes the need for a core team
questions.answer: It can adjust labour costs quickly
questions.hint: Think about which costs can rise or fall easily.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which term describes the extent to which a manager retains ultimate accountability after delegating a task?
questions.hint: It is the part of the job that is not passed on.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: State the name of the structure in which staff report to both a functional manager and a project manager.
questions.hint: Think of a grid.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Explain two reasons why core employees in a shamrock organization may be more motivated than those in the flexible labour force.
questions.hint: Compare job security, pay or involvement in decisions.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Analyse how a change from a tall hierarchy to a project-based organization could affect internal communication.
questions.hint: Consider both speed and possible confusion.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A film production company employs most of its crew only for the length of each film. Evaluate the use of a project-based, shamrock-type structure for this company.
questions.hint: Consider flexibility, costs, quality and morale, then reach a judgement.

bus-sl.topic: Organizational structure: hierarchy, span of control and delegation

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What does an organization chart show?
options: The formal structure of authority and reporting in a business
The market share of a business
The marketing plan of a business
questions.answer: The formal structure of authority and reporting in a business
questions.hint: Think about who reports to whom.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: State the term for the number of subordinates directly accountable to one manager.
questions.hint: It describes how wide a manager's direct responsibility stretches.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: State the term for the line through which authority passes from the top of a hierarchy to the bottom.
questions.hint: Orders travel along it.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which of the following best defines delegation?
options: Passing authority for a task to a subordinate
Moving a business to another country
questions.answer: Passing authority for a task to a subordinate
questions.hint: A manager gives someone else the power to act.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which feature is typical of a tall organizational structure?
options: Many levels of hierarchy and narrow spans of control
Few levels of hierarchy and wide spans of control
Employees reporting to two bosses at once
questions.answer: Many levels of hierarchy and narrow spans of control
questions.hint: Picture the shape of the chart.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A business has one managing director, 4 department managers, and 6 employees reporting to each department manager. Calculate the total number of people in the organization.
questions.hint: Add up all three levels.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A hospital ward manager has 3 senior nurses reporting directly to her, and each senior nurse supervises 8 nurses. State the span of control of the ward manager.
questions.hint: Count direct reports only.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: What is meant by centralization?
options: Most decisions are taken by senior managers
Most decisions are taken by local branch staff
Most work is done by external contractors
questions.answer: Most decisions are taken by senior managers
questions.hint: Consider where decision-making power sits.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A likely effect of widening a manager's span of control is that:
options: Each subordinate receives less close supervision
The number of hierarchical levels must rise
questions.answer: Each subordinate receives less close supervision
questions.hint: The manager's time is shared among more people.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Which change is called delayering?
options: Removing one or more levels of a hierarchy
Adding a new level of supervisors
questions.answer: Removing one or more levels of a hierarchy
questions.hint: Think about what happens to the height of the chart.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A matrix structure is best described as one in which:
options: Employees are organized by project teams as well as by function
Decisions are always taken by one owner
There is only one level of hierarchy
questions.answer: Employees are organized by project teams as well as by function
questions.hint: An engineer might also belong to a product team.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A possible disadvantage of a matrix structure is:
options: Employees may have conflicting instructions from two managers
Teams cannot be created for projects
questions.answer: Employees may have conflicting instructions from two managers
questions.hint: Think about who an employee answers to.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: State the term for the transfer of decision-making authority away from head office to lower levels of an organization.
questions.hint: It is the opposite of keeping decisions at the top.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Explain two advantages to a growing retailer of delegating decisions to its store managers.
questions.hint: Consider both the store managers and senior leaders.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: Using the concept of span of control, explain why a flat structure may suit a small software company.
questions.hint: Think about communication and the type of employee.

questions.subject: bus
questions.q: A family-owned restaurant chain is opening 20 new branches. Discuss whether it should become more decentralized.
questions.hint: Weigh local knowledge against consistency of the brand.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: An element with the configuration [Ar] 4s² is found in:
questions.hint: The principal quantum number and the number of outer electrons give the position.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: State the atomic number of the element in period 3, group 13.
questions.hint: Count across from sodium.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which species has the smallest radius?
questions.hint: These ions are isoelectronic, so compare nuclear charges.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which correctly compares the radii of a chlorine atom and a chloride ion?
options: The Cl⁻ ion is larger than the Cl atom
The Cl atom is larger than the Cl⁻ ion
questions.answer: The Cl⁻ ion is larger than the Cl atom
questions.hint: Consider repulsion when an electron is added.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Why is the first ionisation energy of aluminium lower than that of magnesium?
options: The outer electron of Al is in a higher-energy 3p sub-level
Al has a smaller nuclear charge than Mg
The outer electron of Al is in the 3s sub-level
Al has more electron shells than Mg
questions.answer: The outer electron of Al is in a higher-energy 3p sub-level
questions.hint: Compare the sub-levels from which the electrons are removed.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Why is the first ionisation energy of sulfur lower than that of phosphorus?
options: Repulsion between paired electrons in a 3p orbital
Sulfur has a lower nuclear charge
Sulfur has a smaller shell of electrons
Phosphorus has its outer electrons in the 3d sub-level
questions.answer: Repulsion between paired electrons in a 3p orbital
questions.hint: Draw the 3p orbitals as boxes for each element.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: State the oxidation state of phosphorus in P₄O₁₀. Give your answer as a number without a sign.
questions.hint: Oxygen is usually −2.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: State the oxidation state of sulfur in SO₃. Give your answer as a number without a sign.
questions.hint: Oxygen is usually −2.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which equation correctly shows phosphorus(V) oxide reacting with water?
questions.hint: The product is a phosphoric acid; check the balance.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which is the correct equation for sodium reacting with water?
questions.hint: Check that both hydrogen and sodium are balanced.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: State the trend in reactivity with water going down group 1.
questions.hint: Think about how easily the outer electron is lost.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which halogen is the strongest oxidising agent?
questions.hint: Consider which atom best attracts an extra electron.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which mixture would produce a displacement reaction?
questions.hint: A more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive halide.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: State the colour of iodine dissolved in a non-polar solvent such as hexane.
questions.hint: It looks quite different from its aqueous colour.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Explain, with reference to ionisation energy, why potassium reacts more vigorously with water than sodium.
questions.hint: Link atomic size, shielding and how easily the electron is lost.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Explain why period 3 oxides change from ionic to covalent across the period, and describe the effect on the pH of the solutions they form.
questions.hint: Use the electronegativity difference with oxygen.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: The elements in the same period of the periodic table have the same number of:
questions.hint: Think about what row number tells you.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: State the number of valence electrons in an atom of a group 16 element.
questions.hint: Look at the last digit of the group number.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: State the block of the periodic table in which sodium is found.
questions.hint: Consider the sub-level of its outermost electron.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: An element has the electron configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p³. State its period number.
questions.hint: Look at the highest principal quantum number.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which element has the largest atomic radius?
questions.hint: All four are in period 3.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Why does atomic radius decrease from left to right across period 3?
options: Nuclear charge increases while shielding stays similar
Electrons are added to new shells
questions.answer: Nuclear charge increases while shielding stays similar
questions.hint: Compare the pull of the nucleus with the shielding.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which equation represents the first ionisation energy of sodium?
questions.hint: Pay attention to the state symbols.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: State the trend in first ionisation energy down group 1.
questions.hint: Consider how far the outer electron is from the nucleus.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which element has the highest electronegativity?
questions.hint: It is at the top of its group, near the right of its period.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Why does electronegativity decrease down group 17?
options: The bonding electrons are further from the nucleus and more shielded
Nuclear charge decreases down the group
The atoms have more valence electrons
questions.answer: The bonding electrons are further from the nucleus and more shielded
questions.hint: Think about the size of the atom.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Which period 3 oxide is amphoteric?
questions.hint: It reacts with both acids and bases.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What forms when sodium oxide reacts with water?
questions.hint: Metal oxides usually give alkaline solutions.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: What forms when sulfur trioxide dissolves in water?
questions.hint: Non-metal oxides often give acidic solutions.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: State the acid–base nature of magnesium oxide.
questions.hint: Think about the type of element bonded to oxygen.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Explain why the first ionisation energy generally increases across period 3.
questions.hint: Consider nuclear charge, shielding and distance.

questions.subject: chem
questions.q: Describe the trend in the acid–base character of the oxides across period 3, and explain it in terms of bonding.
questions.hint: Compare the oxides at each end of the period.
